findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (form): B and D are the two options that carry an explanatory clause (B: 'a flat fish being the wrong shape for a square'; D: 'so the extra size did not give a round fish its width') and B is the longest option; A and C are bare procedural claims

justification: Form and domain knowledge together narrow to B or D, roughly even; I picked D as the premise-type statement ('what is said about the cod end'). Calibration: the form channel is student-available; the mesh-geometry knowledge is not something a Swedish 18-year-old would have.

findings: ENTAILMENT (stem-to-option, near): 'bound twice' all but presupposes a second indenture running past the point the first would have ended, so A is derivable from the stem without the passage unless the second binding was only for the remainder of the first term

findings: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE (domain, översilning/silängar): a silängs main channel runs along the upper edge with a fall gentler than the meadow below so water spills evenly; C states exactly this geometry

findings: MIRRORED_TWIN: C is B with the causal arrow reversed (B: oxygen in the running water speeds peat decomposition and frees nutrients; C: peat decomposition consumes the water's oxygen 'och frigjorde på så sätt näring') and C is incoherent on its own (consuming oxygen is not a mechanism that releases nutrients); the twin advertises that oxygen/peat-mineralisation is the tested mechanism and B is the coherent member

PAIR_STRUCTURE: A and D are the two 'the water itself fertilised the mire' variants (silt vs dissolved nutrients), leaving B/C as the one mechanistic pair; 'huvudorsaken' in the stem signals the text ranks a non-obvious mechanism above the folk explanations
WORLD_KNOWLEDGE (domain): modern accounts of silängar on peat attribute yield gains chiefly to oxygen-driven mineralisation, not silt or nutrient-poor brook water
justification: B is answerable blind. Calibration: the mirrored-twin route is form-only and student-available (C's causal chain is visibly broken); domain knowledge independently confirms B.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (semantic fit): an 'överenskommelse' between farms sharing an irrigated mire is most naturally about the order in which they may take the water (D) or how the hay was divided (B); A (how long the meadows were in use) would need a second date and C (how many dagsverken the digging took) is not what an agreement records

justification: D at roughly 50-55 percent with B the live alternative; I cannot see what the writer actually uses the 1858 document for. Mostly student-available reasoning about what an agreement would contain.
